transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Carlos (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood CSM); Lena (PeakWave Head of ML), Marcus (Platform), Anika (Procurement), Samir (SRE)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in to discuss renewal terms, add committed capacity, and scope a short APAC edge pilot. Customer wants predictable latency in APAC and a plan for private networking (VPC) + KMS for keys. They raised cost vs latency tradeoffs and want a short benchmark during pilot. Next steps agreed include pricing, pilot runbook, and onboarding workshop.

Topics: renewal terms, committed capacity tiers, APAC edge pilot, VPC/private deployment questions, KMS/encryption, SLOs and fallbacks, procurement timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Carlos (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making the time. Quick roll call real fast. Carlos from Redwood, Priya our solutions engineer, Ethan our CSM.
[00:12] Lena (PeakWave - Head of ML): Hi all, Lena here.
[00:15] Marcus (Platform Eng): Marcus on the call.
[00:18] Anika (Procurement): Anika.
[00:20] Samir (SRE): Samir, SRE.
[00:22] Carlos: Great. The agenda, we'll do a short renewal recap, discuss capacity uplift options, then focus on the APAC edge pilot details and any security/compliance asks. Does that work?
[00:32] Lena: Sounds good. Quick context, our renewal hits end of September. We're running prod now in NA, and we need to add APAC low-latency region for a new feature launch in Q4. We're also evaluating cost tradeoffs, so want committed pricing vs on-demand.
[00:46] Carlos: Yup, understood. Priya, do you want to take us through the capacity/architecture options?
[00:50] Priya (Redwood SE): Sure. Thanks. So there are two main levers: dedicated reserved pools (what we call Redwood Dedicated) for predictable throughput, and hosted with burst for spiky loads. For APAC low-latency we recommend a small dedicated pool in the region for baseline QPS, with burst routing to hosted or other regions as fallback. That keeps tail latency down.
[01:12] Marcus: Question — how do we do VPC peering for the private deployment? We need traffic to stay on our network for tokens that touch PII models.
[01:20] Priya: For Private deployments we offer a VPC option where the control plane is customer-managed; for Dedicated we can provide VPC peering and private-peering options. There is a quick setup doc, but key things: you need a dedicated NAT and routes, and we support customer-managed KMS for keys at rest.
[01:38] Samir: On KMS — do you support HSM-backed keys or just cloud KMS?
[01:42] Priya: We support cloud KMS (GCP/AWS) and HSM via integration partners. HSM is part of our Private package; we'll share the compliance matrix.
[01:51] Lena: Good. On performance — we need 99th percentile latency below 120ms for the reranking model in APAC. Is that achievable with the small dedicated pool?
[02:02] Priya: It depends on sequence lengths and batching. If you pin a model variant with quantization and tune batch sizes we routinely hit sub-100ms p99 for mid-sized seq lengths on edge GPUs. But we should bench with your prompt set.
[02:17] Marcus: We'll probably have 1.2k QPS peak for inference and heavy KV cache reuse. Does Redwood handle KV cache warmup across nodes?
[02:26] Priya: Yes, we have KV cache management and automatic prefix caching. For multi-node pools, some warmup is expected; we can pre-warm using a synthetic workload in the pilot. We'll include a warmup script in the runbook.
[02:38] Lena: Can we talk pricing options?
[02:41] Carlos: Sure — main options: 1) hosted on-demand — per-token pricing; 2) 12-month committed Reserved capacity with a monthly commit (discounted unit prices); 3) Dedicated with a baseline monthly commit plus overage. For APAC edge we'd recommend a 3-month trial commit and then move to annual once latency verified.
[03:02] Anika: Procurement wants clear PO terms — can you send a renewal amendment that has committed units, skateboard? sorry, that last was me — 'scaling' I mean.
[03:12] Carlos: Yes — I will send an amendment showing tiered committed levels (small / med / large) with corresponding unit pricing. We'll also include zone failover terms and an SLA appendix.
[03:21] Anika: Also need SOC 2 Type II and ISO doc and encryption detail.
[03:26] Ethan (Redwood CSM): We'll share SOC 2 and ISO certs, our audit summary, and the data flow whitepaper. We'll also put in the KMS/HSM detail and retention options.
[03:36] Marcus: Are there any gotchas if we want private endpoints inside our VPC? Latency wise and routing?
[03:41] Priya: Private endpoints add a small network hop; in APAC if you colocate a dedicated pool in-region the impact is minimal. The bigger gotcha is DNS and cert rollover — we'll coordinate with your infra on cert rotation windows.
[03:55] Samir: For observability we need token-level cost visibility and per-route tracing. Does the console support that out of the box?
[04:03] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token breakdown and traces. We can enable higher retention for logs as an add-on. We'll share a sample dashboard export.
[04:13] Lena: On the pilot itself, we want to run two models: a reranker and a short-form generator. The reranker is the tight p99 SLA. We expect to start a 3-week pilot in August. What's the minimum we need from us to make it realistic?
[04:28] Priya: Minimum: sample prompt set (~500 queries) reflecting peak QPS, your model binaries or weights (or we can serve compatible variants), network access for pre-warm scripts, and a dedicated test environment. We'll provide the benchmark harness and a perf template.
[04:42] Lena: We'll provide prompts and the weights — but we may prefer Redwood to host the model binary. Any IP concerns?
[04:48] Carlos: We have model onboarding terms in the MSA that cover customer-owned model assets. For Private deployments we can keep binaries entirely within your VPC. For hosted/Dedicated, we can accept customer-provided weights under our data handling addendum — we'll share the language.
[05:02] Marcus: One more thing — latency fallbacks. If APAC dedicated pool is saturated, can requests automatically route to NA with more permissive latency? We want graceful degradation rather than errors.
[05:12] Priya: Absolutely — smart routing rules exist. You can set policy: prefer region, then fallback to other region with a latency threshold, or fallback to a lower-cost quantized model. We'll include example policies.
[05:26] Anika: Procurement timeline: we need final numbers within two weeks to align with our internal budgeting.
[05:31] Carlos: We can do that. I'll send an updated pricing and a recommendation for committed tier by 2026-08-02.
[05:37] Lena: Cool. About benchmarks — do you have a public GPU perf sheet to compare against Anthropic or Vertex?
[05:43] Priya: We publish model performance profiles, but vendor-to-vendor comparatives are tricky because of different prompt sets. We'll share our benchmark sheet and the pilot harness so you can run apples-to-apples.
[05:55] Samir: Any compliance or onboarding docs you can drop now?
[05:58] Ethan: Yes, I'll drop links: SOC 2 summary, ISO certs, network runbook, onboarding checklist, and the APAC pilot runbook.
[06:06] Marcus: For the APAC nodes — what hardware are we looking at? A2 versus A10?
[06:10] Priya: For low-latency reranking we recommend A10-like or equivalent edge GPUs. We also have quantized 4-bit paths that can reduce memory/cost. We'll propose hardware in the runbook based on your model sizes.
[06:23] Lena: Great. Any blockers from your side?
[06:26] Carlos: No blockers. We'll need confirmation from Marcus on expected QPS and whether you want HSM.
[06:32] Marcus: I can get that over by next week.
[06:35] Anika: We'll need pricing and contract terms to legal before 8/10 ideally.
[06:40] Carlos: Noted. We'll aim to get draft amendment and pricing in two business days.
[06:44] Priya: I'll also prep the perf harness and a warmup script so you can pre-warm KV cache before cutover.
[06:50] Lena: One last question — do you support multi-tenant isolation if we run multiple product lines?
[06:55] Priya: Yes, we can partition token-level quotas, RBAC, and per-route routing. For stronger isolation you'd go Dedicated pools per product.
[07:06] Carlos: Okay let's recap action items and owners...
[07:10] Ethan: I'll book the technical onboarding for week of 8/9 once Marcus confirms QPS.
[07:15] Carlos: I'll send the pricing amendment and committed tiers by 8/2.
[07:18] Priya: I'll share APAC pilot runbook, perf harness, warmup scripts, and a sample policy for fallback routing by 8/3.
[07:26] Marcus: I'll send infra topology and QPS numbers by 8/6.
[07:30] Anika: Procurement will review and revert with PO process by 8/10.
[07:35] Lena: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the pilot.
[07:38] Carlos: Thanks all — we'll follow up via email with links.
